_provenance: AUTHORED source of truth for the book's metaphor spans — where each metaphor is introduced and where it pays off — so the editorial rule 'never introduce a second metaphor until the first has paid off' is MEASURABLE. book-models/metaphor_spans_model.py projects the inventory and computes overlaps, wired into `catalog.py validate` (structural BLOCKING; overlap AUDIT-ONLY-first). Edit a span HERE. Anchors are heading/index-def/point slugs (stable across prose edits), NOT line numbers; re-resolve an anchor with `python3 book-models/metaphor_spans_model.py anchors`.
overlap_rule: A LOCAL metaphor must pay off before the next LOCAL metaphor is introduced within the same stretch. CORE vocabulary (the Printer, churn, map-and-territory, the Model Zoo, the loop, the engineer's seat) is always live and exempt. Overlap = two locals in one stretch whose [introduced_at, pays_off_at] spans intersect. Any real overlap must be ratified (overlap_ok:true + a rationale on either party) or it is a finding.

metaphors.name: The Printer
metaphors.vehicle: a 3D printer, not a coder or a stapler
metaphors.payoff: A bad build indicts the instructions, not the machine.
metaphors.notes: The governing metaphor. Boundary named in 1.3 (loops-and-models); revisited at the close in 6.3-conclusion. Sub-images (stapler, CAD/slicing, the open-ended-technology siblings) belong to this cluster, not separate rows.

metaphors.name: Churn
metaphors.payoff: The wall a fleet hits; the governed environment pushes it back.
metaphors.notes: Named as recurring vocabulary on the glossary page (ground truth for core). Cashed as an empirical curve in 5.2-the-timeline-and-the-work (anchor churn): peaks at mechanization, then collapses.

metaphors.name: Engineering capital
metaphors.vehicle: financial capital that earns compounding interest, not error that snowballs
metaphors.payoff: The stock the positive dual of churn accrues; it earns returns while it stays fit, and depreciates when it does not.
metaphors.notes: The vehicle for the compounding principle — attached to the STOCK (engineering capital), so flow (compounding) and stock stay coherent. Named on the glossary page (ground truth for core); pays off in Part 6 (the increasing-returns proposition + the Bureaucracy-vs-Engineering-capital section, where technical debt is set against engineering capital). Compound INTEREST, deliberately: it fixes the valence against the pre-existing opposite-sign term `compounding-failure-probability` (Part 4). No vehicle collision — no prior `capital`/`compound` span exists.

metaphors.name: Map and territory
metaphors.vehicle: a map drops detail and is not the land
metaphors.payoff: Justifies the drift and parity gates that keep map equal to territory.
metaphors.notes: Named on the glossary page (ground truth for core). Does real work in 2.2-models-and-the-semantic-gap (anchor map-and-territory): model is the map, code the territory, hand-sync drifts.

metaphors.name: The Model Zoo
metaphors.vehicle: a zoo of executable models on tour
metaphors.payoff: The 4+1 views, each walked as a drift-gated model over real code.
metaphors.notes: Named on the glossary page (ground truth for core). Opens and carries all of Part 3, from 3.1-the-executable-zoo (anchor model-zoo) onward.

metaphors.name: The loop
metaphors.payoff: Agent work is a loop you engineer at four control points.
metaphors.notes: "Nearly everything in this book is an instance of it." The four levers land in 1.3; recurs book-wide.

metaphors.name: The engineer's seat
metaphors.vehicle: two seats — the engineer's and the developer's
metaphors.payoff: The developer's seat moves to the fleet; humans keep the engineering seats.
metaphors.notes: Classed core (medium confidence): anchors chapter 1.5 and is cashed in the back matter (6.2-implications-for-se). If read as a chapter-local frame, reclassify local — it is then the sole local in 1.5 (still no overlap).

metaphors.name: The reasoning horizon
metaphors.vehicle: a horizon bounding how much reasoning state a task can hold at once
metaphors.payoff: Models extend the horizon; MAGE moves the wall, it does not remove it.
metaphors.notes: Core vocabulary from 1.1 onward: the reasoning-horizon reframe of the Modeling Thesis recurs across the preface, 1.4, 2.3, 3.1/3.7, and the theory chapter's Reasoning-Horizon Proposition (6.0). Sub-images 'reasoning state' and 'working memory' belong to this cluster, not separate rows. Spatial vehicle named once, then used plainly (the define-once discipline).

metaphors.name: The search space
metaphors.vehicle: agent behavior as a search over a vast space
metaphors.payoff: A model aims the search and shrinks what must be held.
metaphors.notes: Sole local in 1.3; co-occurs only with the core loop (exempt).

metaphors.name: Poka-yoke / the fixture
metaphors.vehicle: a jig that will not seat a bad part
metaphors.payoff: Mistake-proofing: shape the work so the defect cannot happen.
metaphors.notes: Pays off in place, in the paragraph that raises it.

metaphors.name: The raven and the pebbles
metaphors.vehicle: Aesop's raven raising water to reach it
metaphors.payoff: A goal-directed agent takes indirect steps toward a target.
metaphors.notes: Pays off in the paragraph that defines the agent.

metaphors.name: The evidence staircase
metaphors.payoff: Cheap checks early bind an exact tree; later stages check the binding instead of trusting a self-report.
metaphors.notes: Vehicle word 'staircase' is reused by mage-staircase (5.4) — see the vehicle-collision check. Renaming this to 'the evidence ladder/ratchet' (a DEFERRED editorial call, no content edit here) would free 'staircase' for the load-bearing 5.4 close.

metaphors.name: The diffusion analogy
metaphors.payoff: On novel code the average pull is against you; impose the bias yourself.
metaphors.notes: Pays off in the section that raises it.

metaphors.name: Jugaad
metaphors.payoff: Engineering converts a successful improvisation into a durable mechanism.
metaphors.notes: "MAGE begins where jugaad ends." Pays off in the same passage.

metaphors.name: The coin
metaphors.payoff: Fuzzing and property testing draw one oracle from one spec.
metaphors.notes: Carried by the figure 'The Coin Is the Model' in the same section.

metaphors.name: The DOJ ramp
metaphors.vehicle: call-ahead-for-a-ramp versus the ramp is simply there
metaphors.payoff: Accessibility as a property present by default, not requested on demand.
metaphors.notes: The DOJ's own analogy, carried in the burden-shift table.

metaphors.name: The MAGE staircase
metaphors.vehicle: a five-rung climb of delegated jobs
metaphors.payoff: Each rung fixes what broke the rung below; the climb ends at MAGE.
metaphors.notes: The book's structural climb; shares the vehicle word 'staircase' with evidence-staircase (2.3), a different Part.
